title: North Phoenix residents capture moments inside car during hailstorm
text: North Phoenix residents capture moments inside car during hailstorm Locals share their harrowing experiences after massive hail pummeled their vehicles. Residents say they have never experienced a storm quite like it. until THU 10:00 PM MST, Upper Gila River and Aravaipa Valleys including Clifton\/Safford, Galiuro and Pinaleno Mountains including Mount Graham, White Mountains of Graham and Greenlee Counties including Hannagan Meadowuntil FRI 12:00 AM MDT, Chuska Mountains and Defiance Plateau, Black Mesa Area, Chinle Valley, Northeast Plateaus and Mesas Hwy 264 Northward, Northeast Plateaus and Mesas South of Hwy 264until THU 11:00 PM MST, Northwest Plateau, Oak Creek and Sycamore Canyons, Marble and Glen Canyons, Eastern Mogollon Rim, Coconino Plateau, Yavapai County Valleys and Basins, Little Colorado River Valley in Navajo County, White Mountains, Grand Canyon Country, Western Mogollon Rim, Yavapai County Mountains, Little Colorado River Valley in Apache County, Kaibab Plateau, Northern Gila County, Little Colorado River Valley in Coconino County North Phoenix residents are dealing with widespread damage and shattered windows following a severe hailstorm. A mother and daughter recorded video from inside their car as golf ball-sized hail cracked their windshield. Santa Velazquez and her daughter, Alessandra Ullmer, had just returned from a doctor's appointment and were waiting for the rain to pass before heading inside when the storm intensified on Oct. 21. Video recorded from inside their car captured the pair screaming as golf ball-sized hail struck the vehicle, denting its body and cracking the windshield.Ullmer said she feared the windshield would give way.\"I thought it was going to fall down too, so I put my legs up, and I was like, a little scared. But it was definitely scary seeing cracks all over and over each time it hit and just hearing all the thumps. It was very loud, and I'm very loud in the video, but it was very loud outside too,\" Ullmer said. Residents are facing days of repairs after a severe storm left dented vehicles and shattered windows.One family captured the scary moments on video. The storm caused widespread damage across North Phoenix, leaving residents with broken windows, dented vehicles and repairs ahead. Richard Stevenson, a Phoenix resident whose car was also pummeled by hail, said the noise caught him by surprise.\"All of a sudden, I'm hearing boom, boom, boom, boom, boom ... \" Stevenson said. \"I thought Jesus was throwing baseballs at us. \"\"I thought windows were going to break.I was thinking the ceiling was gonna fall in. Like, it was crazy. I ain't never experienced nothing like it,\" Stevenson said. While severe weather tracked through northern and eastern Arizona, Phoenix saw sunny skies with warm, mild temperatures heading into the weekend.Velazquez said she was grateful that she and her daughter were not driving when the hail struck. Although repairs lie ahead, she said their safety was what mattered most.\"This is material. Like my mom says, you know, every negative comes with a positive. So I know there's a positive. I just don't know what it is yet, but there is a positive,\" Velazquez said.Information in this report was gathered from Santa Velazquez, caught in the hail storm; Alessandra Ullmer, caught in the hail storm; and Richardson Stevenson, a Phoenix resident.
